2122.subject: Zoology
2122.text: The shoulder blade is made of
2122.sol: Scapula (shoulder blade) is the largest of the bones that make up each half of the pectoral (shoulder) girdle. It is a flat triangular bone, providing anchorage for the muscles of the forelimb and an articulation for the humerus at the glenoid cavity. It is joined to the clavicle (collar bone) in front. Clavicle is a bone that forms part of the pectoral (shoulder) girdle, linking the scapula (shoulder blade) to the stemum (breast bone). In humans it forms the collar bone and serves as a brace for the shoulders. Humerus is the long bone of the upper arm which articulates with the scapula (shoulder blade) at the glenoid cavity and with the ulna and radius (via a condyle) at the elbow. Ilium is the largest of the three bones that make up each half of the pelvic girdle. The ilium bears a flattened wing of bone that is attached by ligaments to the sacrum.

&=-193+\frac{300 \times 100}{1000} \\
&=-193+30 \\
& \Delta \mathrm{H}^{{}^{\circ}}=-163 \mathrm{ kJ} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$

4655.subject: Chemistry
4655.text: Arrange the following oxides in correct order of their acidic character.
4655.sol:
Acidic character of oxides in group 15 to 18 elements decreases down the group. As we move down the group, the atomic size increases and electronegativity decreases. The oxide in the higher oxidation state of the elements is more acidic than that of lower oxidation state. In $\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_3(\mathrm{I}), \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ (II) and $\mathrm{As}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ (IV), N, $P$ and As are in +3 oxidation state respectively whereas in $\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5$ (III) the $\mathrm{N}$ is in +5 oxidation state. So, the acidity order is

$\mathrm{N}}_{2}  \mathrm{O}$}_{5}>$\mathrm{N}}_{2}  \mathrm{O}$}_{3}>$\mathrm{P}}_{2}  \mathrm{O}$}_{3}>$\mathrm{As}}_{2}  \mathrm{O}$}_{3} $\text{, i.e. } \mathrm{III}$>$\mathrm{I}$>$\mathrm{II}$>$\mathrm{IV}$

6221.text: The stationary points of the curve $y = 8x^{2} - x^{4} - 4$& are____
6221.sol:
Given curve& $y = 8x^{2} - x^{4} - 4$

Differentiate on both sides

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 16x - 4x^{3}$

To get stationary points~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$4x\left(4 - x^{2}\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 0, x^{2} = 4$

$⇒ x = 0, \pm 2$

$x = 0 ⇒ y = 8\left(0\right) - 0 - 4 = - 4$

$x = 2 ⇒ y = 8\left(4\right) - 16 - 4 = 12$

$x = - 2 ⇒ y = 8\left(4\right) - 16 - 4 = 12$

So required stationary points are~$\left(0, - 4\right), \left(2, 12\right), \left(- 2, 12\right) .

&

7060.text: Suppose that the circle \(x²+y²+2 g x+2 f y+c=0\) has its centre on \(2 x+3 y-7=0\) and cuts the circles \(x²+y²-4 x-6 y+11=0\) and \(x²+y²-10 x-4 y+21=0\) orthogonally. Then \(5 g-10 f+3 c=\)
7060.sol:
The equation of given circle
\(x²+y²+2 g x+2 f y+c=0\) ...(i)
having centre \((-g,-f)\) lying on the line
$\begin{aligned} \text{$ and $} 2 x+3 y-7=0 \\ \text{ and } \text{so }2 g+3 f+7=0 \quad \ldots (ii)
\end{aligned}\)
Since circle (i) cuts the given circles
\(\quad \begin{aligned}x²+y²-4 x-6 y+11 & =0 \\
\text{and }x^2+y²-10 x-4 y+21 & =0
\end{aligned}\)
orthogonally
\($\begin{array}{lc}$\text{ so, }$& 2 g(-2)+2 f(-3)=c+11 \\
\Rightarrow & 4 g+6 f+c+11=0 \quad \ldots (iii) \\
$\text{$ and }& 2 g(-5)+2 f(-4=c+21 \\
\Rightarrow & 10 g+4 f+c+21=0 \quad \ldots (iv) \end{array} From $Eqs. (iii) and (iv), we get
\(6 g-2 f+10=0 \quad \ldots (v) \)
From Eq. (ii) and (v), we get
\(\begin{gathered}11 f+11=0 \Rightarrow f=-1 \\
\text{So, } g=-2 \Rightarrow c=3
\end{gathered}\)\begin{aligned}& \therefore 5 g-10 f+3 c=5(-2)-10(-1)+3(3) \\
& =-10+10+9=9
\end{aligned} \)
Hence, option (4) is correct.$

10768.text: A die is tossed thrice. If event of getting an even number is a success, then the probability of getting at least $2$ successes is
10768.sol:
Let $X$ denotes the& number of successes in $3$ trials. Then, $X$ is a binomial variate with $n = 3$,

$p = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Then, $P ( X = r ) = Cr 3 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)r, r = 0, 1, 2, 3$

Therefore, the required probability of getting at least two successes is

$P ( X \ge 2 ) = P ( X = 2 ) + P ( X = 3 )$

$= C2 3 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3} + C3 3 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3}$

$= 3 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3} + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3}$

$= \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3} \times 4$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}$

10824.text: An envelope is known to have come from either 'LONDON' or 'CLIFTON'. On the postal mark only two successive letters ON are legible. The probability that the envelope comes from LONDON is
10824.sol:
According to the given information, the number of two successive letters in word LONDON is 5, similarly in word CLIFTON is 6.

Let event $E_1$ is selecting word LONDON and event $E_2$ is selecting word CLIFTON.

So, $P\left(E_1\right)=\frac{1}{2}$ and $P\left(E_2\right)=\frac{1}{2}$
and the event $A$ is getting successive letter ON.
Then, $P\left(A / E_1\right)=\frac{2}{5}$ and $P\left(A / E_2\right)=\frac{1}{6}$.
$\therefore$ Required probability,

P$\left(\frac{E_1}{A}\right)=\frac{P\left(E_1\right) \cdot P\left(\frac{A}{E_1}\right)}{P\left(E_1\right) \cdot P\left(\frac{A}{E_1}\right)+P\left(E_2\right) \cdot P\left(\frac{A}{E_2}\right)}

\begin{aligned}$& =$\frac{\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{5}}{\left(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{5}\right)+\left(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{6}\right)}=\frac{\frac{2}{5}}{\frac{2}{5}+\frac{1}{6}}$\\
& =$\frac{2 \times 6}{12+5}=\frac{12}{17}
\end{aligned}$Hence, option (a) is correct.

12954.text: If $\theta \in [ 0, 2\pi ]$ and $cos2\theta = cos\theta + sin\theta$ then the sum of all values of $\theta$ satisfying the equation is
12954.sol:

Using, $cos2A = {cos}^{2}x - {sin}^{2}x$, we get

${cos}^{2}\theta - {sin}^{2}\theta = cos\theta + sin\theta$

$⇒ cos\theta + sin\theta = 0$ or $cos\theta - sin\theta = 1$

Now, $cos\theta + sin\theta = 0 ⇒ cos\theta = - sin\theta$

$⇒ tan\theta = - 1$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}$

And, $cos\theta - sin\theta = 1$

Either $cos\theta = 1, sin\theta = 0$

$⇒ \theta = 0, 2\pi$

Or $cos\theta = 0$, $sin\theta = - 1$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$

Now, Sum of all possible values of $\theta$ is $\dfrac{3\pi}{4} + \dfrac{7\pi}{4} + 0 + 2\pi + \dfrac{3\pi}{2} = \dfrac{24\pi}{4}$

In a right angle triangle, in $\triangle A B C \begin{aligned} A C² & =A B²+B C² \\ \Rightarrow \quad A C & =\sqrt{A B^2+B C^2}=\sqrt{\left(4 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2+\left(3 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2}\\ \Rightarrow \quad A C & =5 \times10^{-2} \mathrm{ m} \end{aligned}$ Initial electric potential energy of three charges, $\begin{aligned} U & =\frac{k q_1 q_2}{A B}+\frac{k q_1 q_3}{A C}+\frac{k q_2 q_3}{B C}\\ & =\frac{k\left(4 \times 3 \times 10^{-12}\right)}{4 \times 10^{-2}}+\frac{k\left(4 \times 5 \times 10^{-12}\right)}{5 \times 10^{-2}}+\frac{k\left(3 \times 5 \times 10^{-12}\right)}{3 \times 10^{-2}}\\ & =k\left[3 \times10^{-10}+4 \times10^{-10}+5 \times10^{-10}\right] \\ & =9 \times10^9 \times12 \times10^{-10} \\ & =108 \times10^{-1}=10.8 \mathrm{ J} \end{aligned}$ \\ When three charges located of an equilateral triangle of side $3 \mathrm{ cm}$, the final potential energy of three charges system, $\begin{gathered} =\frac{k q_1 q_2}{A B}+\frac{k q_2 q_3}{B C}+\frac{k q_1 q_3}{A C}$\\ =$\frac{k\left(4 \times 3 \times 10^{-12}\right)}{3 \times 10^{-2}}+\frac{k\left(3 \times 5 \times 10^{-12}\right)}{3 \times 10^{-2}}+\frac{k\left(4 \times 5 \times 10^{-12}\right)}{3 \times 10^{-2}}$\\ =$\frac{9 \times 10^9}{3}\left[12 \times10^{-10}+15 \times10^{-10}+20 \times10^{-10}\right]=14.1 \mathrm{ J} \end{gathered}$ Hence, the work done in moving charges at points A and C, W=(14.1-10.8)=3.3 $\mathrm{ J} .$

21607.subject: Mathematics
21607.text: If $X = \tan^{-1} \left[2\cos \left(2\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right] + \cos^{-1}\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)\right]$ and $Y = \sin^{-1} \left[\sin \left(\dfrac{11\pi}{6}\right)\right] + \tan^{-1}\left[\tan\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)\right]$ then the value of $2X - Y$ is:
21607.sol:
Evaluating the first expression $X$:

$\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$\tan^{-1}\left[2\cos\left(2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\right] = \tan^{-1}\left[2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\right] = \tan^{-1}\left(2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right) = \tan^{-1}(1) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

For the second term of $X$, the principal value branch of $\cos^{-1}$ is $[0, \pi]$:

$\cos^{-1}\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)\right] = \cos^{-1}\left[\cos\left(2\pi - \dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)\right] = \cos^{-1}\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)\right] = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$

Thus, $X = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{5\pi}{6} = \dfrac{13\pi}{12}$

Evaluating the second expression $Y$:

The principal value branch of $\sin^{-1}$ is $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$:

$\sin^{-1}\left[\sin\left(\dfrac{11\pi}{6}\right)\right] = \sin^{-1}\left[\sin\left(2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right] = \sin^{-1}\left[-\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right] = -\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

The principal value branch of $\tan^{-1}$ is $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$:

$\tan^{-1}\left[\tan\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)\right] = \tan^{-1}\left[\tan\left(\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\right] = \tan^{-1}\left[\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\right] = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Thus, $Y = -\dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Calculating $2X - Y$:

$2X - Y = 2\left(\dfrac{13\pi}{12}\right) - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{13\pi}{6} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{12\pi}{6} = 2\pi$

Answer: $2\pi$

22174.subject: Mathematics
22174.text: The equation of a line passing through origin with direction angles $\dfrac{2 \pi}{3}$, $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $\dfrac{\pi}{3} is$
22174.sol:
The direction angles of the line are given as $\alpha = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, $\beta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, and $\gamma = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

The direction cosines of the line are $l = \cos \alpha$, $m = \cos \beta$, and $n = \cos \gamma$.

Calculating these values:
$l = \cos \left( \dfrac{2\pi}{3} \right) = -\dfrac{1}{2}$
$m = \cos \left( \dfrac{\pi}{4} \right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$n = \cos \left( \dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

The equation of a line passing through the origin $(0, 0, 0)$ with direction cosines $(l, m, n)$ is given by $\dfrac{x}{l} = \dfrac{y}{m} = \dfrac{z}{n}$.

Substituting the values:
$\dfrac{x}{-1/2} = \dfrac{y}{1/\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{z}{1/2}$

Multiplying the denominators by $2$:
$\dfrac{x}{-1} = \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{z}{1}$

This can be rewritten as:
$-x = \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{2}} = z$

Multiplying by $-1$:
$x = \dfrac{y}{-\sqrt{2}} = -z$

Answer: $x=\dfrac{y}{-\sqrt{2}}=-z$

In series $L-C-R$ circuit,

$\begin{aligned}$X_{L} &=X_{C} \\
\therefore \quad & Z=$\sqrt{R^{2}+\left(X_{L}-X_{C}\right)^{2}}
\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}$&=$\sqrt{R^{2}+0^{2}}$\\
Z &=R \\
\therefore $\text{ Power factor }$&=\cos \phi \\
&=$\frac{R}{Z}=\frac{R}{R}=$1
\end{aligned}

Hence, power factor is not zero.
Therefore option (d) is not correct.$ In L-C-R$ series resonance circuit, peak energy stored by a capacitor is equal to peak energy stored by an inductor.
Average power, $P_{\mathrm{avg}}=V_{\mathrm{rms}} \times I_{\mathrm{rms}} \times \cos 0^{{}^{\circ}} \begin{aligned}$&=V_${\text{rms }} \times$I_${\text{rms }}$ \\
&=$\text{ apparent power }
\end{aligned}L-C-R$ series resonance circuit is purely resistive because $X_{L}=X_{C}$, hence no wattless current exists in this circuit therefore wattless current is zero.

23348.subject: Physics
23348.text: A ray of light is travelling from glass of refractive index $\dfrac{3}{2}$ to water of refractive index $\dfrac{4}{3}$. What is the minimum angle of incidence for which no light enters in to the water?
23348.sol:
The condition for no light to enter the water is that the angle of incidence must be greater than or equal to the critical angle $i_c$.

The critical angle $i_c$ is defined by the relation $\sin(i_c) = \dfrac{\mu_{rarer}}{\mu_{denser}}$.

Given the refractive index of glass $\mu_g = \dfrac{3}{2}$ and the refractive index of water $\mu_w = \dfrac{4}{3}$.

Since $\mu_g > \mu_w$, the light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium.

Substituting the values into the formula:

$\sin(i_c) = \dfrac{\mu_w}{\mu_g} = \dfrac{4/3}{3/2} = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{8}{9}$.

Therefore, $i_c = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{8}{9}\right)$.

Answer: $i_c=\sin ^{-1}\left(\dfrac{8}{9}\right)$

23406.text: $0.04 \mathrm{ m}$ of glass contains the same number of waves as $0.05 \mathrm{ m}$ of water, when monochromatic light passes through them normally. Refractive index of water is $4 / 3$. Refractive index of glass is
23406.sol:
If $n$ be the number of waves, then wavelength of light in glass, $\lambda_{g}=\frac{0.04}{n}$ and wavelength of light in water, $\lambda_{w}=\frac{0.05}{n}$ Speed of light in glass, $v_{g}=\lambda_{g} \times f=\frac{0.04 f}{n}$ where, $f=$ frequency of light.
Similarly, speed of light in water, $v_{w}=\lambda_{w} \times f=\frac{0.05 f}{n}$
Relative refractive index
$\begin{aligned}
&=\frac{\mu_{w}}{\mu_{g}}=\frac{v_{g}}{v_{w}}=\frac{0.04 f}{n} \times \\
&=\frac{5}{4} \times \mu_{w}=\frac{5}{4} \times \frac{4}{3}=\frac{5}{3}
\end{aligned}$

23664.subject: Physics
23664.text: A light having wavelength $6400^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{A}$ is incident normally on a slit of width $2 \mathrm{ mm}$. Then the linear width of the central maximum on the screen kept $2 \mathrm{ m}$ from the slit is :
23664.sol:
The width of the central maximum in a single slit diffraction pattern is given by the formula $w = \dfrac{2 \lambda D}{a}$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of light, $D$ is the distance of the screen from the slit, and $a$ is the width of the slit.

Given values are:
$\lambda = 6400 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m} = 6.4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$
$D = 2 \text{ m}$
$a = 2 \text{ mm} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$

Substituting these values into the formula:
$w = \dfrac{2 \times (6.4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}) \times (2 \text{ m})}{2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}}$

$w = \dfrac{25.6 \times 10^{-7}}{2 \times 10^{-3}} \text{ m}$

$w = 12.8 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$

$w = 1.28 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m} = 1.28 \text{ mm}$

Answer: 1.28 mm

26713.text: Young’s modulus of elasticity $Y$ is expressed in terms of three derived quantities, namely, the gravitational constant $G$, Planck’s constant $h$ and the speed of light $c$, as $Y = {c}^{\alpha}{h}^{\beta}{G}^{\gamma}$. Which of the following is the correct option?
26713.sol:
Dimensions of Young's modulus: $\left[{M}^{1}{L}^{– 1}T{}^{– 2}\right]$

Dimensions of velocity of light: $\left[{M}^{0}{L}^{1}{T}^{– 1}\right]$

Dimensions of Planck's constant: $\left[{M}^{1}{L}^{2}{T}^{– 1}\right]$

Dimensions of Gravitational constant: $\left[{M}^{– 1}{L}^{3}{T}^{– 2}\right]$

Now, as given in the question$

$Y = {c}^{\alpha}{h}^{\beta}{G}^{\gamma}$

$⇒ $\left[{M}^{1}{L}^{– 1}T{}^{– 2}\right]$ = {$\left[{M}^{0}{L}^{1}{T}^{– 1}\right]$}^{\alpha}{$\left[{M}^{1}{L}^{2}{T}^{– 1}\right]$}^{\beta}{$\left[{M}^{– 1}{L}^{3}{T}^{– 2}\right]$}^{\gamma}$

Comparing exponent of the M, L & T both sides, we get$

$1 = \beta - \gamma ⇒ \beta = 1 + \gamma . . . \left(1\right)$

$- 1 = \alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma . . . \left(2\right)

and $- 2 = - \alpha - \beta - 2\gamma . . .$\left(3\right)$

From equation(1) and (2), we get$

$- 1 = \alpha + 2$\left(1 + \gamma\right) + 3\gamma ⇒ \alpha + 5\gamma = - 3 . . . \left(4\right)

From equation(1)$ and (3), we get

$- 2 = - \alpha - \left(1 + \gamma\right) - 2\gamma ⇒ \alpha + 3\gamma = 1 . . . \left(5\right)

From equation(4)$ and equation(5), we get

$\alpha = 7, \gamma = – 2$ and then $\beta = 1 + \gamma = - 1$.

34634.subject: Mathematics
34634.text: Let $y = y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $(\tan x)^{1/2}\,dy = (\sec^3 x - (\tan x)^{3/2} y)\,dx$, $0 < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{6\sqrt{2}}{5}$. If $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{4}{5}\alpha$, then $\alpha^4$ equals _______.
34634.sol:
The given differential equation can be rewritten as:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + (\tan x)y = \dfrac{\sec^3 x}{(\tan x)^{1/2}}$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x)$.

Integrating Factor (IF) = $e^{\int \tan x \, dx} = e^{\ln(\sec x)} = \sec x$

Multiplying both sides by the IF and integrating, we get:

$y \sec x = \int \dfrac{\sec^4 x}{(\tan x)^{1/2}} \, dx + C$

$y \sec x = \int \dfrac{(1 + \tan^2 x)\sec^2 x}{(\tan x)^{1/2}} \, dx + C$

Let $\tan x = t$, then $\sec^2 x \, dx = dt$.

$y \sec x = \int \dfrac{1 + t^2}{t^{1/2}} \, dt + C$

$y \sec x = \int (t^{-1/2} + t^{3/2}) \, dt + C$

$y \sec x = 2t^{1/2} + \dfrac{2}{5}t^{5/2} + C$

$y \sec x = 2(\tan x)^{1/2} + \dfrac{2}{5}(\tan x)^{5/2} + C$

Given $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{6\sqrt{2}}{5}$, substituting $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$:

$\dfrac{6\sqrt{2}}{5} \cdot \sqrt{2} = 2(1)^{1/2} + \dfrac{2}{5}(1)^{5/2} + C$

$\dfrac{12}{5} = 2 + \dfrac{2}{5} + C \Rightarrow C = 0$

The solution is $y \sec x = 2(\tan x)^{1/2} + \dfrac{2}{5}(\tan x)^{5/2}$.

Substituting $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$:

$y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) \cdot 2 = 2(\sqrt{3})^{1/2} + \dfrac{2}{5}(\sqrt{3})^{5/2}$

$y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 3^{1/4} + \dfrac{1}{5} \cdot 3^{5/4} = 3^{1/4}\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{5}\right) = \dfrac{8}{5} \cdot 3^{1/4}$

Given $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{4}{5}\alpha$, we have:

$\dfrac{4}{5}\alpha = \dfrac{8}{5} \cdot 3^{1/4} \Rightarrow \alpha = 2 \cdot 3^{1/4}$

Therefore, $\alpha^4 = (2 \cdot 3^{1/4})^4 = 16 \cdot 3 = 48$

Answer: $48$

35468.text:
Consider the system of equations :
$x+a y=0, y+a z=0$ and $z+a x=0$. Then the set of all real values of ' $a$ ' for which the system has a unique solution is:
35468.sol:
Given system of equations is homogeneous which is

$\begin{aligned}$&x+a y=0 \\
&y+a z=0 \\
&z+a x=0
\end{aligned}

It can be written$ in matrix form as\mathrm{A}=\left(\begin{array}{lll}1 & a & 0 \\
0 & 1 & a \\
a & 0 & 1
\end{array}$\right)

Now, $|\mathrm{A}|=\left[1-a\left(-a^2\right)\right]=1+a^3 \neq 0$
So, system has only trivial solution.
Now, $|\mathrm{A}|=0$ only when $a=-1$
So, system of equations has infinitely many solutions which is not possible because it is given that system has a unique solution.
Hence set of all real values of ' $a$ ' is

$\mathrm{R}-$\{-1\}

36857.text: Let $a, b, c$ be the length of three sides of a triangle satisfying the condition $\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right){x}^{2} - 2b\left(a + c\right) x + \left({b}^{2} + {c}^{2}\right) = 0$. If the set of all possible values of $x$ is in the interval $\left(\alpha, \beta\right),$ then $12\left({\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2}\right)$ is equal to _______.
36857.sol:
Given,

$\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right){x}^{2} - 2b\left(a + c\right)x + {b}^{2} + {c}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ {a}^{2}{x}^{2} - 2abx + {b}^{2} + {b}^{2}{x}^{2} - 2bcx + {c}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ {\left(ax - b\right)}^{2} + {\left(bx - c\right)}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ ax - b = 0, bx - c = 0$

$⇒ ax = b, bx = c$

Now, we know that the sum of two sides is always greater than the third side of a triangle,

Now, taking $a + b > c$ we get,

$⇒ a + ax > bx$

$⇒ a + ax > a{x}^{2}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - x - 1 < 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 - \sqrt{5}}{2} < x < \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2} . . . \left(i\right)$

Similarly, for $b + c > a$ we get,

$⇒ {x}^{2} + x - 1 > 0$

$⇒ x \in \left(- \infty , \dfrac{- 1 - \sqrt{5}}{2}\right) ∪ \left(\dfrac{- 1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}, \infty\right) . . . . \left(ii\right)$

And for $c + a > b$ we get,

$⇒ {x}^{2} - x + 1 > 0$

$⇒ x \in R . . . . . . . . \left(iii\right)$

So, from the equation $\left(i\right), \left(ii\right) \text{ and } \left(iii\right)$ we get,

$x \in \left(\dfrac{- 1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}, \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{\sqrt{5} - 1}{2}, \beta = \dfrac{\sqrt{5} + 1}{2}$

Hence, $12\left({\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2}\right) = 12\left(\dfrac{{\left(\sqrt{5} - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(\sqrt{5} + 1\right)}^{2}}{4}\right) = 36$

37376.text: Let $A = \{2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$. Let R be a relation on the set $A \times A$ given by $(x, y) R (z, w)$ if and only if $x$ divides $z$ and $y \leq w$. Then the number of elements in R is _______.
37376.sol:
Given the set $A = \{2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$.

The relation $R$ is defined on $A \times A$ such that $(x, y) R (z, w)$ if and only if $x$ divides $z$ and $y \leq w$.

The number of elements in $R$ is the number of ordered pairs $((x, y), (z, w))$ satisfying these conditions. Since the conditions for $(x, z)$ and $(y, w)$ are independent, the total number of elements in $R$ will be the product of the number of pairs $(x, z)$ satisfying $x$ divides $z$ and the number of pairs $(y, w)$ satisfying $y \leq w$.

First, we find the number of pairs $(x, z) \in A \times A$ such that $x$ divides $z$:
For $x = 2$, $z \in \{2, 4, 6\}$ ($3$ pairs)
For $x = 3$, $z \in \{3, 6\}$ ($2$ pairs)
For $x = 4$, $z \in \{4\}$ ($1$ pair)
For $x = 5$, $z \in \{5\}$ ($1$ pair)
For $x = 6$, $z \in \{6\}$ ($1$ pair)
Total number of pairs $(x, z) = 3 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8$.

Next, we find the number of pairs $(y, w) \in A \times A$ such that $y \leq w$:
For $y = 2$, $w \in \{2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$ ($5$ pairs)
For $y = 3$, $w \in \{3, 4, 5, 6\}$ ($4$ pairs)
For $y = 4$, $w \in \{4, 5, 6\}$ ($3$ pairs)
For $y = 5$, $w \in \{5, 6\}$ ($2$ pairs)
For $y = 6$, $w \in \{6\}$ ($1$ pair)
Total number of pairs $(y, w) = 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 15$.

The total number of elements in the relation $R$ is the product of the number of these pairs:
Total elements = $8 \times 15 = 120$.

Answer: $120$

37719.text: If the sum of squares of all real values of $\alpha$, for which the lines $2x - y + 3 = 0, 6x + 3y + 1 = 0$ and $\alpha x + 2y - 2 = 0$ do not form a triangle is $p$, then the greatest integer less than or equal to $p$ is ________.
37719.sol:
Given lines are $2x - y + 3 = 0$, $6x + 3y + 1 = 0$ and $\alpha x + 2y - 2 = 0$.

These lines will not form a triangle if $\alpha x + 2y - 2 = 0$ is concurrent with $2x - y + 3 = 0$ and $6x + 3y + 1 = 0$ or parallel to either of them.

Case-$1$: Concurrent lines

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}2 & - 1 & 3 \\ 6 & 3 & 1 \\ \alpha & 2 & - 2\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 2\left(- 6 - 2\right) + 1\left(- 12 - \alpha\right) + 3\left(12 - 3\alpha\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 16 - 12 - \alpha + 36 - 9\alpha = 0$

$⇒ - 10\alpha + 8 = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Case-$2$: Parallel lines

$\dfrac{- \alpha}{6} = \dfrac{- 2}{3}$, $- \dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{- 2}{- 1}$

$⇒ \alpha = 4$, $\alpha = - 4$

$⇒ P = 16 + 16 + \dfrac{16}{25}$

$[ P ] = \left[32 + \dfrac{16}{25}\right] = 32$

40274.text: An electromagnetic wave travels in free space along the $x$-direction. At a particular point in space and time, $\vec{B} = 2 \times 10^{-7} \hat{j}$ T is associated with this wave. The value of corresponding electric field $\vec{E}$ at this point is _______ V/m.
40274.sol:
The direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave is given by the direction of $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.

Given that the wave travels along the $x$-direction, the direction of propagation is $\hat{i}$.

The magnetic field is given as $\vec{B} = 2 \times 10^{-7} \hat{j}$ T, so its direction is $\hat{j}$.

Let the direction of the electric field be $\hat{n}$. We must have:

$\hat{n} \times \hat{j} = \hat{i}$

Since $(-\hat{k}) \times \hat{j} = \hat{i}$, the direction of the electric field is $-\hat{k}$.

The magnitude of the electric field is related to the magnetic field by $E = cB$, where $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s is the speed of light in free space.

$E = (3 \times 10^8) \times (2 \times 10^{-7}) = 60$ V/m

Therefore, the electric field vector is $\vec{E} = -60 \hat{k}$ V/m.

Answer: $-60 \hat{k}$

40442.subject: Physics
40442.text:
Identify the correct statements :
A. Electrostatic field lines form closed loops.
B. The electric field lines point radially outward when charge is greater than zero.
C. The Gauss - Law is valid only for inverse - square force.
D. The workdone in moving a charged particle in a static electric field around a closed path is zero.
E. The motion of a particle under Coulomb's force must take place in a plane.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
40442.sol:
Statement A: Electrostatic field lines originate from positive charges and terminate on negative charges. They do not form closed loops because the electrostatic field is conservative. Thus, A is incorrect.
Statement B: For a positive point charge ($q > 0$), the electric field lines are directed radially outwards. Thus, B is correct.
Statement C: Gauss's Law is a consequence of the inverse-square nature of Coulomb's law ($F \propto 1/r^2$). If the force law were different, Gauss's Law would not hold in its standard form. Thus, C is correct.
Statement D: The electrostatic field is conservative, meaning the work done in moving a charge along any closed path is zero ($\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{l} = 0$). Thus, D is correct.
Statement E: Coulomb's force is a central force. The motion of a particle under a central force always takes place in a plane because the torque about the center is zero, keeping angular momentum constant in direction. Thus, E is correct.
Since B, C, D, and E are correct, the correct option is (4).

From the statements given below :

(A) The angular momentum of an electron in ${n}^{th}$ orbit is an integral multiple of $h$.

(B) Nuclear forces do not obey inverse square law.

(C) Nuclear forces are spin dependent.

(D) Nuclear forces are central and charge independent.

(E) Stability of nucleus is inversely proportional to the value of packing fraction.

42522.sol:
(A) Electron revolves around nucleus only in those orbits for which the angular momentum is an integral multiple of $\dfrac{h}{2\pi}$.

(B) Nuclear force does not follow the inverse square law.

(C) Nuclear forces are spin dependent but charge independent.

(D) Nuclear force is attractive in nature. It is a non central force, meaning it does not depend upon the distance between the particles but rather upon their orientation. Nuclear force is stronger if the spin is parallel; and weak if it is anti parallel.

(E) The negative value (less quantity) of packing fraction indicates that the isotope is stable. Positive value of packing fraction implies unstable (radioactive) nucleus. Also, the stability of the nucleus is inversely proportional to the value of the packing fraction.

In figure (a), the springs are connected in series. Therefore,

${K}_{eq} = \dfrac{{K}_{1}{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1} + {K}_{2}} = \dfrac{K \times 2K}{K + 2K} = \dfrac{2K}{3}$

Therefore, the time period

${T}_{a} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{{K}_{eq}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{\dfrac{2K}{3}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{3m}{2K}}$

In figure (b), the springs are connected in parallel. Therefore,

${K}_{eq} = {K}_{1} + {K}_{2} = 3K$

Therefore, the time period

${T}_{b} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{{K}_{eq}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{3K}}$

Now,

$\dfrac{{T}_{a}}{{T}_{b}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{2}} ⇒ {T}_{b} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}{T}_{a} = \sqrt{2}s$

Hence, $x = 2$

42864.subject: Physics
42864.text:
A convex lens of refractive index 1.5 and focal length $f=18 \mathrm{~cm}$ is immersed in water. The difference in focal lengths of the given lens when it is in water and in air is $\alpha \times \mathrm{f}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
(refractive index of water $=4 / 3$)
42864.sol:
Using the lensmaker's equation, in air:
$\frac{1}{f_{air}} = (n - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)$ where $(n-1) = 0.5$ for glass with $n = 1.5$.
In water:
$\frac{1}{f_{water}} = \left(\frac{n}{n_{water}} - 1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)$
$= \left(\frac{1.5}{4/3} - 1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)$
$= \frac{1}{8}\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)$
Since $\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right) = \frac{2}{f_{air}} = \frac{2}{18}$,
We get $\frac{1}{f_{water}} = \frac{1}{8} \cdot \frac{2}{18} = \frac{1}{72}$, so $f_{water} = 72$ cm.
The difference is $f_{water} - f_{air} = 72 - 18 = 54$ cm.
Therefore $\alpha = \frac{54}{18} = 3$.

43148.subject: Physics
43148.text: A solid sphere ($A$) of mass $5m$ and a spherical shell ($B$) of mass $m$, both having same radius, are placed on a rough surface. When a force of same magnitude is applied tangentially at the highest points of $A$ and $B$, they start rolling without slipping with an acceleration of $a_A$ and $a_B$, respectively. The ratio of $a_A$ and $a_B$ is __________.
43148.sol:
For a body of mass $M$ and radius $R$ rolling without slipping under a force $F$ applied tangentially at the highest point, the torque about the point of contact with the ground is $\tau = F(2R)$.

The moment of inertia about the point of contact is $I = I_{cm} + MR^2$.

Using $\tau = I\alpha$ and the rolling without slipping condition $a = \alpha R$, we get:

$F(2R) = (I_{cm} + MR^2) \dfrac{a}{R} \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{2FR^2}{I_{cm} + MR^2}$

For the solid sphere $A$ of mass $5m$:

$I_{cm,A} = \dfrac{2}{5}(5m)R^2 = 2mR^2$

$a_A = \dfrac{2FR^2}{2mR^2 + 5mR^2} = \dfrac{2F}{7m}$

For the spherical shell $B$ of mass $m$:

$I_{cm,B} = \dfrac{2}{3}mR^2$

$a_B = \dfrac{2FR^2}{\dfrac{2}{3}mR^2 + mR^2} = \dfrac{2F}{\dfrac{5}{3}m} = \dfrac{6F}{5m}$

The ratio of their accelerations is:

$\dfrac{a_A}{a_B} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2F}{7m}}{\dfrac{6F}{5m}} = \dfrac{2}{7} \times \dfrac{5}{6} = \dfrac{5}{21}$

Answer: $5 : 21$

43429.subject: Physics
43429.text: A diode has Zener voltage of $10$ V and maximum power dissipation of $0.5$ W, then the minimum resistance to be used in series with this diode for safety when it is connected to a $25$ V power supply is ______ $\Omega$.
43429.sol:
Given Zener voltage $V_Z = 10$ V and maximum power dissipation $P_{max} = 0.5$ W.

The maximum safe current through the Zener diode is given by $I_{max} = \dfrac{P_{max}}{V_Z} = \dfrac{0.5}{10} = 0.05$ A.

The voltage drop across the series resistor is $V_R = V_S - V_Z = 25 - 10 = 15$ V.

For safety, the current through the circuit should not exceed $I_{max}$. Thus, the minimum resistance $R$ is $R = \dfrac{V_R}{I_{max}} = \dfrac{15}{0.05} = 300$ $\Omega$.

Answer: $300$

43701.text: A thin rod having a length of $1m$ and area of cross-section $3 \times {10}^{- 6}{m}^{2}$ is suspended vertically from one end. The rod is cooled from $210 ° C$ to $160 ° C$. After cooling, a mass $M$ is attached at the lower end of the rod such that the length of rod again becomes $1m$. Young's modulus and coefficient of linear expansion of the rod are $2 \times {10}^{11}N{m}^{- 2}$ and $2 \times {10}^{- 5}{K}^{- 1}$, respectively. The value of $M$ is ______ $kg$. (Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
43701.sol:
Let $\Deltal$ be the decease in length of rod due to decease in temperature

Then, $\Deltal = l\alpha\DeltaT$, here, coefficient of linear expansion is $\alpha = 2 \times {10}^{- 5}{K}^{- 1}$ and $\DeltaT = ( 483 - 433 ) K$$= 50K$

Thus, $\Deltal = 1 \times 2 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 50 = {10}^{- 3}m$

Young's modulus is stated as $Y = \dfrac{\dfrac{F}{A}}{\dfrac{\Deltal}{l}}$, here, $F = Mg$.

So, $2 \times {10}^{11} = \dfrac{Mg \times 1}{3 \times {10}^{- 6} \times {10}^{- 3}}$

$⇒ Mg = 2 \times {10}^{11} \times 3 \times {10}^{- 9} = 6 \times {10}^{- 2}$

Thus, $M = 60kg$

46249.text: At what distance (in metre) from the centre of the Moon, the intensity of gravitational field will be zero? (Take, mass of Earth and Moon as $5.98 \times 10^{24} \mathrm{~kg}$ and $7.35 \times 10^{22} \mathrm{~kg}$ respectively and the distance between Moon and Earth is $3.85 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m}$.)
46249.sol:
Let X be the distance of the point from the centre of earth where gravitational intensity is zero. Therefore,
$\frac{\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}}}{\mathrm{x}^2}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{m}}}{\left(3.85 \times 10^8-\mathrm{x}\right)^2}$
or $\frac{\mathrm{x}}{3.85 \times 10^8-\mathrm{x}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{e}}}{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{m}}}}=\sqrt{\frac{5.98 \times 10^{24}}{7.35 \times 10^{22}}} \cong 9$
or $\quad \frac{x}{9}+x=3.85 \times 10^8$
or $\quad \mathrm{x}=9 \times 3.85 \times 10^8 / 10=3.46 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m}$
Distance from Moon $=3.85 \times 10^8-3.46 \times 10^8$
$=3.9 \times 10^7 \mathrm{~m} \cong 3.85 \times 10^7 \mathrm{~m}$

48727.text: The least positive integer $\mathrm{n}$, for which $\frac{(1+i)^{n}}{(1-i)^{n-2}}$ is positive, is
48727.sol:
$\begin{aligned} \frac{(1+i)^{\mathrm{n}}}{(1-\mathrm{i})^{\mathrm{n}-2}} &=\left(\frac{1+\mathrm{i}}{1-\mathrm{i}}\right)^{\mathrm{n}}(1-\mathrm{i})^{2} \\ &=\left(1+\mathrm{i}^{2}-2 \mathrm{i}\right)\left(\frac{1+\mathrm{i}}{1-\mathrm{i}}\right)^{\mathrm{n}} \\ &=(1-1-2 \mathrm{i})\left(\frac{1+\mathrm{i}}{1-\mathrm{i}}\right)^{\mathrm{n}} \\ &=(-2 \mathrm{i})\left(\frac{1+\mathrm{i}}{1-\mathrm{i}}\right)^{\mathrm{n}} \end{aligned} \begin{aligned}&=(-2 i)\left\{\frac{(1+i)(1+i)}{(1-i)(1+i)}\right\}^{n} \\
&=(-2 i)\left\{\frac{2 i}{2}\right\}^{n}\quad\left(\because \mathrm{i}^{2}=-1\right) \\
&=(-2 i)(i)^{\mathrm{n}} \\
&=(-2) i^{n+1}
\end{aligned} Put \mathrm{n}=1$, we get $\begin{aligned}&=(-2) i^{2}=(-2)(-1) \\
&=2 \Rightarrow \text{ positive integer. }
\end{aligned}$ Hence, the least positive integer value of $n=1$ for which the given expression have positive value.

59127.subject: Chemistry
59127.text:
Vapour pressure of $\text{CCl}_4$ at $25^{}^{\circ}$ C is $143$ mm Hg. If $0.5$ g of a non-volatile solute is dissolved in $100 \text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{CCl}_4$. Find the vapour pressure of the solution.
(Density of $\text{CCl}_4 = 1.58 \text{ g}/\text{cm}^3$ and molecular weight of solute is $65$)
59127.sol:
Mass of solvent ($CCl_4$), $W_1 = \text{Volume} \times \text{Density} = 100 \times 1.58 = 158 \text{ g}$

Molar mass of $CCl_4$, $M_1 = 12 + 4(35.5) = 154 \text{ g/mol}$

Number of moles of solvent, $n_1 = \dfrac{W_1}{M_1} = \dfrac{158}{154} \approx 1.026$

Mass of solute, $W_2 = 0.5 \text{ g}$

Molar mass of solute, $M_2 = 65 \text{ g/mol}$

Number of moles of solute, $n_2 = \dfrac{W_2}{M_2} = \dfrac{0.5}{65} \approx 0.0077$

According to Raoult's law, the relative lowering of vapour pressure is given by:

$\dfrac{P^0 - P_s}{P^0} = \dfrac{n_2}{n_1 + n_2}$

$\dfrac{143 - P_s}{143} = \dfrac{0.0077}{1.026 + 0.0077}$

$\dfrac{143 - P_s}{143} = \dfrac{0.0077}{1.0337} \approx 0.00745$

$143 - P_s = 143 \times 0.00745 \approx 1.065$

$P_s = 143 - 1.065 = 141.935 \text{ mm Hg}$

59393.subject: Chemistry
59393.text: The ratio of mass of 'x' atoms of an element to mass of carbon atoms is 9:1. Find the mass of 1 mol of x if molar mass of carbon is 12 g/mol.
59393.sol:
Let the mass of one atom of element 'x' be $m_x$ and the mass of one carbon atom be $m_C$.

Given that the ratio of the mass of an atom of element 'x' to the mass of a carbon atom is $9:1$, we have:

$\dfrac{m_x}{m_C} = \dfrac{9}{1}$

The ratio of their molar masses is equal to the ratio of their atomic masses:

$\dfrac{M_x}{M_C} = 9$

Given the molar mass of carbon, $M_C = 12\ \text{g/mol}$, the molar mass of element 'x' is:

$M_x = 9 \times 12 = 108\ \text{g/mol}$

Therefore, the mass of $1\ \text{mol}$ of element 'x' is $108\ \text{g}$.

59926.subject: Chemistry
59926.text: Which from following reactions is exothermic?
59926.sol:
The reaction is exothermic when it releases heat, indicated by a negative enthalpy change ($\Delta H < 0$).

Neutralization between a strong base and strong acid, such as $\mathrm{KOH}_{(\mathrm{aq})} + \mathrm{HNO}_{3(\mathrm{aq})} \rightarrow \mathrm{KNO}_{3(\mathrm{aq})} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, is highly exothermic.

Melting ice ($\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{(s)} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{(l)}$) is endothermic, requiring energy input. Dissolution of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ ($\mathrm{NaCl}_{(\mathrm{s})} + \mathrm{aq} \rightarrow \mathrm{Na}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+} + \mathrm{Cl}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{-}$) is slightly endothermic with a net heat absorption. Formation of $\mathrm{NO}_2$ from elements ($\mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 2\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NO}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$) is endothermic, as confirmed by its positive standard enthalpy of formation.

Only option A is exothermic.

Answer: $\boxed{A}$

61011.text: If $\int\limits_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}(\sin^2 x + \sin^3 x)dx = k$, then the value of $k$
61011.sol:
Let $I = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} (\sin^2 x + \sin^3 x) dx$

$I = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x dx + \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \sin^3 x dx$

Since $\sin^3 x$ is an odd function, $\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \sin^3 x dx = 0$

Since $\sin^2 x$ is an even function, $\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x dx = 2 \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x dx$

$I = 2 \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x dx = 2 \left( \dfrac{\pi}{4} \right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Therefore, $k = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

61299.subject: Mathematics
61299.text: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y + 5$ and $y(0) = 4$ then $y(\log 2)$ is equal to
61299.sol:
Given differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y + 5$

Separating the variables gives

$\dfrac{dy}{y + 5} = dx$

Integrating both sides gives

$\int \dfrac{dy}{y + 5} = \int dx$

$\log|y + 5| = x + C$

Using the initial condition $y(0) = 4$ gives

$\log(4 + 5) = 0 + C \Rightarrow C = \log 9$

Substituting $C$ back into the equation gives

$\log(y + 5) = x + \log 9$

$y + 5 = e^{x + \log 9} = 9e^x$

$y = 9e^x - 5$

Substituting $x = \log 2$ gives

$y(\log 2) = 9e^{\log 2} - 5$

$y(\log 2) = 9(2) - 5 = 13$

Answer: $13$

\therefore \quad & \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=-\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)^{\mathrm{k}-1} \\
& \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}+\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^{1-\mathrm{k}}=0 \\
& \text{ But } \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}+\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}=0 ...[Given]
\end{aligned}$ Comparing above equations, we get
$\begin{aligned}
1-k & =\frac{1}{3} \\
& 1-\frac{1}{3}=k \\
\therefore \quad k & =\frac{2}{3}

61626.text: If $x = a\sin^3 t$ and $y = a\cos^3 t$, then the value of $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ is equal to
61626.sol:
Given $x = a\sin^3 t$ and $y = a\cos^3 t$.

Differentiating with respect to $t$:

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 3a\sin^2 t \cos t$

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -3a\cos^2 t \sin t$

Now, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\dfrac{dy}{dt}}{\dfrac{dx}{dt}} = \dfrac{-3a\cos^2 t \sin t}{3a\sin^2 t \cos t} = -\cot t$

Differentiating again with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(-\cot t) \cdot \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \csc^2 t \cdot \dfrac{1}{3a\sin^2 t \cos t} = \dfrac{1}{3a\sin^4 t \cos t}$

Substituting $t = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$:

$\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{1}{3a \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^4 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{3a \left(\dfrac{9}{16}\right) \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{32}{27a}$

Answer: $\dfrac{32}{27a}$

62174.text: If $f(x) = \cos x$, then the value of $\int\dfrac{e^{f(x)}(x\sin^3 x + f(x))}{1 - (f(x))^2}dx = $
62174.sol:
Given $f(x) = \cos x$.

Substituting $f(x)$ into the integral, we get:

$I = \int \dfrac{e^{\cos x}(x\sin^3 x + \cos x)}{1 - \cos^2 x} dx$

$I = \int \dfrac{e^{\cos x}(x\sin^3 x + \cos x)}{\sin^2 x} dx$

$I = \int e^{\cos x} \left( x\sin x + \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin^2 x} \right) dx$

$I = \int e^{\cos x} (x\sin x + \text{cosec}\ x \cot x) dx$

We know that $\dfrac{d}{dx} \left( e^{\cos x} g(x) \right) = e^{\cos x} (g'(x) - g(x)\sin x)$.

Let $g'(x) - g(x)\sin x = x\sin x + \text{cosec}\ x \cot x$.

By observation, if we choose $g(x) = -x - \text{cosec}\ x$, then:

$g'(x) = -1 + \text{cosec}\ x \cot x$

$-g(x)\sin x = (x + \text{cosec}\ x)\sin x = x\sin x + 1$

Adding these gives:

$g'(x) - g(x)\sin x = -1 + \text{cosec}\ x \cot x + x\sin x + 1 = x\sin x + \text{cosec}\ x \cot x$.

Thus, the integral evaluates to $e^{\cos x} g(x) + c$.

$I = e^{\cos x} (-x - \text{cosec}\ x) + c$

Substituting back $f(x) = \cos x$:

$I = e^{f(x)} (-\text{cosec}\ x - x) + c$

Answer: $e^{f(x)}(-\text{cosec}\ x - x) + c$

63608.text: If 6 boys and 3 girls are to be seated on chairs for a photograph, then the probability that the end seats are occupied by the girls and no two girls are side by side is
63608.sol:
Total arrangements of 9 distinct individuals are $9! = 362880$.

For favorable arrangements, two girls occupy the end seats: $P(3,2) = 3 \times 2 = 6$ ways. The remaining girl must be placed in a non-adjacent middle seat: 5 valid positions. The 6 boys then arrange in the remaining seats: $6! = 720$ ways.

Thus, favorable outcomes are $6 \times 5 \times 720 = 21600$.

The probability is $\frac{21600}{362880} = \frac{5}{84}$.

64460.text: If the sum of the squares of the distances of a point $P(x, y, z)$ from the three co-ordinate axes is 324 , then the distance of point $P$ from the origin is....
64460.sol:
Distance from the origin: A point $P(x, y, z)$ has an origin distance of $\sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}.

Sum of squared axis distances: The squared distances from the axes are $y^2 + z^2$, $x^2 + z^2$, and $x^2 + y^2$. Their sum is given as 324.

Combine terms: 2x^2 + 2y^2 + 2z^2 = 324$, so $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 162$.

Thus, the distance is $\sqrt{162} = \sqrt{81 \times 2} =9\sqrt{2}.

The correct option is C.

64487.text: The lines $\frac{\mathrm{x}-3}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{y}-2}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-5}{-\mathrm{k}}$ and $\frac{\mathrm{x}-4}{\mathrm{k}}=\frac{\mathrm{y}-3}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-3}{2}$ are coplanar, hence $\mathrm{k}=$
64487.sol:
Coplanarity of two lines occurs when the scalar triple product of the connecting vector and the direction vectors is zero.

Given lines: $\frac{x-3}{1} = \frac{y-2}{1} = \frac{z-5}{-k}$ and $\frac{x-4}{k} = \frac{y-3}{1} = \frac{z-3}{2}$.

The determinant condition is:

$\begin{vmatrix} x_2-x_1 \text{ and } y_2-y_1 \text{ and } z_2-z_1 \\ a_1 \text{ and } b_1 \text{ and } c_1 \\ a_2 \text{ and } b_2 \text{ and } c_2 \end{vmatrix} = 0$

With $P_1(3,2,5)$, $\vec{d_1} = (1,1,-k)$, $P_2(4,3,3)$, $\vec{d_2} = (k,1,2)$, the connecting vector is $(1,1,-2)$.

Substituting yields:

$\begin{vmatrix} 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } -2 \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } -k \\ k \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 2 \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Expanding the determinant:

$1 \cdot (1 \cdot 2 - (-k) \cdot 1) - 1 \cdot (1 \cdot 2 - (-k) \cdot k) + (-2) \cdot (1 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot k) = 0$

$2 + k - (2 + k^2) - 2(1 - k) = 0$

$2 + k - 2 - k^2 - 2 + 2k = 0$

$-k^2 + 3k - 2 = 0$

$k^2 - 3k + 2 = 0$

Factoring gives $(k-1)(k-2) = 0$, so $k = 1$ or $k = 2$.

The lines are coplanar for these values, corresponding to answer choice A.

65868.subject: Physics
65868.text: The electron in hydrogen atom is initially in the second excited state. When it finally moves to ground state, the maximum number of spectral lines emitted are
65868.sol:
The ground state of a hydrogen atom corresponds to the principal quantum number $n = 1$.

The second excited state corresponds to $n = 3$.

The maximum number of spectral lines emitted when electrons transition from an excited state $n$ to the ground state is given by the formula:

Number of spectral lines = $\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}$

Substituting $n = 3$ into the formula:

Number of spectral lines = $\dfrac{3(3-1)}{2} = 3$

The $3$ possible transitions are:
$n = 3 \rightarrow n = 1$
$n = 3 \rightarrow n = 2$
$n = 2 \rightarrow n = 1$

Answer: $3$

66033.text: If the equivalent capacitance between points A and B of the combination of capacitors shown in figure, is 6C, the capacitor $C^1$ is
66033.sol:
The capacitors $2C$, $3C$, and $4C$ are connected in parallel. Their equivalent capacitance is:
$C_p = 2C + 3C + 4C = 9C$

This combination is in series with $C^1$. The total equivalent capacitance between A and B is $6C$.

Using the formula for series combination:
$\dfrac{1}{C_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{C_p} + \dfrac{1}{C^1}$

$\dfrac{1}{6C} = \dfrac{1}{9C} + \dfrac{1}{C^1}$

$\dfrac{1}{C^1} = \dfrac{1}{6C} - \dfrac{1}{9C}$

$\dfrac{1}{C^1} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{18C} = \dfrac{1}{18C}$

$C^1 = 18C$

Answer: $18C$

66794.text: A coil of wire of radius ' $r$ ' has 600 turns and a self-inductance of 108 mH. The self-inductance of a coil with same radius and 500 turns is
66794.sol:
The self-inductance $L$ of a coil is proportional to the square of its number of turns: $L \propto N^2$.

Given initial values $L_1 = 108\text{ mH}$ and $N_1 = 600$, and final turns $N_2 = 500$, the inductance becomes:

$L_2 = L_1 \left(\frac{N_2}{N_1}\right)^2 = 108 \left(\frac{500}{600}\right)^2 = 108 \left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^2 = 108 \cdot \frac{25}{36}$

$L_2 = 3 \cdot 25 = 75\text{ mH}$

Final answer: $75\text{ mH}$

67234.subject: Physics
67234.text: A body is projected vertically from earth's surface with $\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{\text{rd }}$ of escape velocity. The maximum height reached by the body is ( $\mathrm{R}=$ radius of earth)
67234.sol:
Given that the escape velocity from Earth's surface is $v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$, with $G$ the gravitational constant, $M$ the Earth's mass, and $R$ its radius, the body is projected upward with velocity $v = \frac{1}{3}v_e$.

Using conservation of mechanical energy, the initial energy at the surface equals the final energy at maximum height $h$ where velocity is zero:

$\frac{1}{2}mv^2 - \frac{GMm}{R} = -\frac{GMm}{R+h}$

Substituting $v = \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$:

$\frac{1}{2}m \left(\frac{1}{9} \cdot \frac{2GM}{R}\right) - \frac{GMm}{R} = -\frac{GMm}{R+h}$

After simplification, this reduces to:

$\frac{GMm}{9R} - \frac{GMm}{R} = -\frac{GMm}{R+h}$

Dividing through by $GMm$ yields:

$\frac{1}{9R} - \frac{1}{R} = -\frac{1}{R+h}$

Combining the left side gives:

$-\frac{8}{9R} = -\frac{1}{R+h}$

Multiplying both sides by $-1$ and cross-multiplying results in:

$8(R + h) = 9R$

Solving for $h$:

$h = \frac{R}{8}$

Maximum height reached is $\frac{R}{8}$, corresponding to option B.

69202.text: A disc of mass 25 kg and radius 0.2 m is rotating at 240 r.p.m. A retarding torque brings it to rest in 20 second. If the torque is due to a force applied tangentially on the rim of the disc then the magnitude of the force is
69202.sol:
The initial angular speed is $\omega_0 = 240 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = 8\pi \text{rad/s}$, and the disc comes to rest so $\omega = 0$.

Using $\omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t$ with $t = 20\text{s}$ gives $0 = 8\pi + 20\alpha$, leading to $\alpha = -\frac{2\pi}{5}\text{rad/s}^2$, with magnitude $|\alpha| = \frac{2\pi}{5}\text{rad/s}^2$.

The moment of inertia is $I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2 = \frac{1}{2}(25)(0.2)^2 = 0.5\text{kg m}^2$.

The torque is $\tau = I|\alpha| = 0.5 \times \frac{2\pi}{5} = \frac{\pi}{5}\text{N m}$.

Since $\tau = FR$, the force magnitude is $F = \frac{\pi/5}{0.2} = \pi\text{N}$.

69401.subject: Physics
69401.text: In the band structure of n-type semiconductor , the free electrons donated by impurity atoms occupy energy levels in
options: the band gap and are close to conduction band.
the band gap and are close to valence band.
69401.sol:
In an n-type semiconductor, pentavalent impurity atoms are added, which donate extra electrons.

These donated electrons occupy discrete energy levels known as donor energy levels.

The donor energy levels are located in the forbidden energy gap (band gap) just below the bottom of the conduction band (typically $0.01$ eV to $0.05$ eV below it).

Because they are very close to the conduction band, these electrons can easily be excited into the conduction band at room temperature.

Answer: the band gap and are close to conduction band.

70946.subject: Biology
70946.text: Enzymes generally get destroyed at temperature of _______ $^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$.
70946.sol:
Enzymes are typically proteinaceous in nature. At high temperatures, the thermal energy disrupts the non-covalent interactions (like hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds, and hydrophobic interactions) that maintain the complex three-dimensional structure of the protein.

This loss of structural integrity is called denaturation. When denatured, the active site of the enzyme is destroyed, resulting in the loss of catalytic activity.

While different enzymes have different thermal stabilities, most enzymes from mesophilic organisms start to denature and get destroyed at temperatures above $40^{}^{\circ} \text{C}$, and their activity is typically completely lost in the range of $60 - 70^{}^{\circ} \text{C}$.

Therefore, the most appropriate temperature range among the given options at which enzymes generally get destroyed is $60 - 70^{}^{\circ} \text{C}$.

Answer: $60-70$

71056.text: In secondary succession, the species that invades depends on the following EXCEPT:
71056.sol:
Secondary succession occurs in areas where natural biotic communities have been destroyed but soil or sediment is already present.

Since soil is already present, the process does not depend on the development of soil, which is a characteristic of primary succession.

The species that invade during secondary succession depend on the condition of the existing soil, availability of water, the environment, and the types of seeds or other propagules present.

Answer: development of soil.

71712.text:
For the reaction
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}_{(l)} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_{4(g)} + \text{HBr}$, $r = K(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br})$
What is order and molecularity of the reaction respectively ?
71712.sol:
The rate law is given as $r = K[\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}]$.

The order of a reaction is the sum of the exponents of the concentration terms in the rate law. Since the exponent of $[\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}]$ is $1$, the order of the reaction is $1$.

The molecularity of an elementary reaction is the number of reactant molecules taking part in the reaction. In the given reaction, only one molecule of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}$ is reacting, so the molecularity is $1$.

Thus, the order and molecularity are $1$ and $1$ respectively.

Answer: $1, 1$

72070.text:
In an AC circuit, E and I are given by $E = 150\sin(150t)$ V and $I = 150\sin \left(150t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) A. The power dissipated in the circuit is
\{\cos(60)^{}^{\circ} = 1/2\}$

The given equations are $E = 150\sin(150t)$ and $I = 150\sin \left(150t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right).

The peak voltage $ E_0 = 150$ V and the peak current $I_0 = 150$ A.

The phase difference between voltage and current is $\phi = $\dfrac{\pi}{3} =60^{}^{\circ}$.

The average power dissipated in the circuit is given by $P = E_{rms} I_{rms} \cos\phi$.

$P = \dfrac{E_0}{\sqrt{2}} \dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}} \cos\phi = \dfrac{E_0 I_0}{2} \cos\phi

Substituting the values:

$ P = $\dfrac{150 \times 150}{2} \cos(60^{}^{\circ})$

$P = \dfrac{22500}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{22500}{4} =5625$ W.

Answer: $5625\ \text{W}$

72155.subject: Physics
72155.text:
In the case of the photo-electric effect, which of the following sentences is NOT TRUE?
a. The photo-electrons are emitted only when the frequency of incident radiation is greater than the threshold frequency.
b. There is no time lag between incidence of light and emission of electrons.
c. The rate of photo-electric emission is independent of the intensity of incident radiation.
d. The maximum kinetic energy of emitted photo-electrons depends on the frequency of incident radiation.
72155.sol:
According to the laws of photoelectric effect:

1. Photoelectric emission occurs only when the frequency of incident light is greater than the threshold frequency.

2. The process is instantaneous, meaning there is no time lag between the incidence of light and the emission of electrons.

3. The rate of photoelectric emission (number of electrons emitted per second) is directly proportional to the intensity of the incident radiation.

4. The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons depends linearly on the frequency of the incident radiation and is independent of its intensity.

Statement c claims that the rate of photoelectric emission is independent of the intensity of incident radiation, which contradicts the laws of the photoelectric effect. Thus, statement c is not true.

Answer: c

72390.subject: Physics
options: Dark current in photo diode flows only when the photodiode is reverse biased.
Dark current in photo diode is caused by minority carriers flowing across the junction.
Dark current in a photo diode is a small current, typically in the range of picoampere or nanoampere.
Dark current in photo diode is only caused by external background radiation.
72390.sol:
Dark current in a photodiode is the small reverse leakage current that flows when the photodiode is reverse biased and there is no incident light (in complete darkness).

It is caused by the thermal generation of electron-hole pairs in the depletion region, which leads to the flow of minority carriers across the junction. It is not caused by external background radiation.

The magnitude of this current is very small, typically in the range of nanoamperes (nA) or picoamperes (pA).

Therefore, the statement that dark current is only caused by external background radiation is incorrect.

Answer: Dark current in photo diode is only caused by external background radiation.

72495.subject: Physics
72495.text: A sonometer wire vibrating in two loops is in resonance with a tuning fork. If tension applied to the string is increased to 16 times the original tension and length of the wire is doubled. It can still be in resonance with the tuning fork provided it vibrates in
72495.sol:
The frequency of a vibrating string is given by $f = \dfrac{p}{2L} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$, where $p$ is the number of loops, $L$ is the length, $T$ is the tension, and $\mu$ is the linear mass density.

Let the initial frequency be $f_1$. Given $p_1 = 2$, we have:

$f_1 = \dfrac{2}{2L_1} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_1}{\mu}}$

For the final state, the tension is increased to $16$ times the original tension ($T_2 = 16T_1$) and the length is doubled ($L_2 = 2L_1$). The frequency $f_2$ must be equal to $f_1$ for the wire to remain in resonance with the same tuning fork.

$f_2 = \dfrac{p_2}{2L_2} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_2}{\mu}}$

Equating $f_1$ and $f_2$:

$\dfrac{2}{2L_1} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_1}{\mu}} = \dfrac{p_2}{2(2L_1)} \sqrt{\dfrac{16T_1}{\mu}}$

$\dfrac{1}{L_1} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_1}{\mu}} = \dfrac{p_2 \times 4}{4L_1} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_1}{\mu}}$

$\dfrac{1}{L_1} = \dfrac{p_2}{L_1}$

$p_2 = 1$

Therefore, the wire will vibrate in one loop.

Answer: one loop

75351.subject: General Ability
75351.text:
While travelling to a hilly region, you notice a massive boulder, which was loosened by heavy rains and moved downhill. This has resulted due to which of the following processes?
1. Mass wasting
2. Erosion
3. Weathering
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
75351.sol:
Mass wasting is the movement of rock and soil down slope under the influence of gravity. Rock falls, slumps, and debris flows are all examples of mass wasting. Often lubricated by rainfall or agitated by seismic activity, these events may occur very rapidly and move as a flow.
Erosion is the geological process in which earthen materials are worn away and transported by natural forces such as wind or water. A similar process, weathering, breaks down or dissolves rock, but does not involve movement. Weathering is the breaking down or dissolving of rocks and minerals on Earths surface. Once a rock has been broken down, a process called erosion transports the bits of rock and minerals away. Water, acids, salt, plants, animals, and changes in temperature are all agents of weathering and erosion.

80064.subject: Botany
80064.text: In angiosperms, root hairs arise from which one of the following regions of the root ?
80064.sol:
The root is divided into different regions from the apex to the base: the root cap, the region of meristematic activity, the region of elongation, and the region of maturation.

The cells of the elongation zone gradually differentiate and mature to form the region of maturation. From the epidermal cells of the region of maturation, very fine and delicate, thread-like structures called root hairs arise.

These root hairs significantly increase the surface area for the absorption of water and minerals from the soil.

Answer: The region of maturation

80296.subject: Botany
80296.text: Which of the following plant growth regulators is used as herbicide ?
80296.sol:
Plant growth regulators have various physiological functions in plants.

2,4-D (2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid) is a synthetic auxin. It is widely used as a herbicide to kill broad-leaved dicotyledonous weeds in cereal crops and lawns, as it does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants.

Gibberellins are used to promote stem elongation and seed germination.

Kinetin is a cytokinin that promotes cell division.

Abscisic acid is a stress hormone that inhibits growth and promotes seed dormancy.

80836.subject: Chemistry
80836.text: Identify the correct statement about $\text{ClF}_3$ from the following options :
options: It has T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.
It has T-shaped geometry with three lone pairs on Cl atom.
It has a trigonal pyramidal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.
It has a planar trigonal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.
80836.sol:
The central atom in $\text{ClF}_3$ is Chlorine (Cl).

Number of valence electrons of Cl = $7$.

Number of monovalent atoms (F) attached = $3$.

Steric number = $\dfrac{1}{2}(7 + 3) = 5$.

The hybridization of the central atom is $sp^3d$.

Number of bond pairs = $3$.

Number of lone pairs = $5 - 3 = 2$.

The electron geometry is trigonal bipyramidal. According to VSEPR theory, to minimize repulsion, the two lone pairs occupy the equatorial positions.

This results in a T-shaped molecular geometry.

Therefore, $\text{ClF}_3$ has a T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on the Cl atom.

Answer: It has T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.

83601.subject: Physics
83601.text: The temperature of a metallic sphere of radius $R$ is increased by a small amount $\Delta T$. If the linear coefficient of thermal expansion of the metal is $\alpha$, the approximate increase in the volume of the sphere is :
83601.sol:
The initial volume of the metallic sphere is $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3$.

The coefficient of volume expansion $\gamma$ is related to the linear coefficient of thermal expansion $\alpha$ as $\gamma = 3\alpha$.

The increase in volume $\Delta V$ due to a temperature increase $\Delta T$ is given by $\Delta V = V \gamma \Delta T$.

Substituting the values of $V$ and $\gamma$, we get:

$\Delta V = \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3\right)(3\alpha)\Delta T$

$\Delta V = 4\pi R^3\alpha\Delta T$

Answer: $4\pi R^3\alpha\Delta T$

90907.text: Two straight roads $OA$ and $OB$ intersect at $O$. A tower is situated within the angle formed by them and subtends angles of ${45}^{o}$ and ${30}^{o}$ at the points $A$ and $B$ where the roads are nearest to it. If $OA = 400meters$ and $OB = 300meters$, then the height of the tower is

Let, $PQ$ be the tower of height $h.$

Let, $PA, PB$ be the perpendiculars from $P$ upon $OA$ and $OB$ respectively.
Then, $∠PAQ = {45}^{o}$ and $∠PBQ = {30}^{o}$
$OA = 400, OB = 300$
$⇒ \dfrac{PA}{h} = cot ⁡ {45}^{o} = 1 ∴ PA = h$
$⇒ \dfrac{PB}{h} = cot ⁡ {30}^{o} = \sqrt{3} ∴ PB = \sqrt{3}h$
Now, $OP^{2} = PA^{2} + OA^{2} = PB^{2} + OB^{2}$
$⇒ h^{2} + {\left(400\right)}^{2} = 3h^{2} + {\left(300\right)}^{2} ⇒ 2h^{2} = {\left(400\right)}^{2} - {\left(300\right)}^{2}$
$⇒ h = \sqrt{\dfrac{{4}^{2} - {3}^{2}}{2}} \times 100 = 50\sqrt{14}$ meters

$⇒tan\theta = 0$ or $\tan^{2} \theta = 3 = {( \sqrt{3} )}^{2}$

$⇒ \text{tan \theta} = 0 ⇒ \text{\theta} = m\text{\pi ,}m \in I$

94603.subject: Physics
94603.text: Calculate the compressional force required to prevent the metallic rod of length $l cm$ and cross-sectional area $A{cm}^{2}$when heated through $t ° C$, from expanding lengthwise. Young's modulus of elasticity of the metal is $E$ and mean coefficient of linear expansion is $\alpha$& per degree celsius.
94603.sol:
The change in natural length $= \Delta {l ⁡}_{t} = l ⁡ \alpha \text{t}$
The natural length of rod at temperature $t^{∘} \text{C} = l ⁡ + l ⁡ \alpha \text{t}$
The decrease in natural length due to developed stress $= \Delta l ⁡$
But the length of rod remains constant.

$∴ \Delta {l ⁡}_{t} - \Delta l ⁡ = 0$

$∴ \Delta l ⁡ = \Delta {l ⁡}_{t} = l ⁡ \alpha \text{t}$

$∴ \text{E} = \dfrac{\text{stress}}{\text{strain}} = \dfrac{\text{F/A}}{\dfrac{- \Delta l ⁡}{l ⁡ + \Delta {l ⁡}_{t}}}$

$∴ \text{E} = - \dfrac{\text{EA} \Delta l ⁡}{l ⁡ + \Delta {l ⁡}_{t}} = - \dfrac{\text{EA} \Delta {l ⁡}_{t}}{l ⁡ + \Delta {l ⁡}_{t}}$

$= - \dfrac{\text{EA} l ⁡ \alpha \text{t}}{l ⁡ + l ⁡ \alpha \text{t}} = - \dfrac{\text{EA} \alpha \text{t}}{\left(1 + \alpha \text{t}\right)}$

$∵ V ⁡ ( x ) = \dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4} - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}$

at $x = 0$, $V ( x ) = 0$

At $x = \pm 1, ⁡ V ⁡ ( x ) = - \dfrac{1}{4}\text{J}$

$∴ ( \text{Kinetic energy}{)}_{\text{max}} = E{⁡}_{T ⁡} - V{⁡}_{\text{min}}$

or $∴ ( \text{Kinetic energy}{)}_{\text{max}} = 2 + \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{9}{4}\text{J}$

or $\dfrac{1}{2}m ⁡ {ν}_{m ⁡}^{2} = \dfrac{9}{4}$

${ν}_{\text{m}}^{2} = \dfrac{9 \times 2}{\text{m} \times 4}$

or ${ν}_{m ⁡}^{2} = \dfrac{9 \times 2}{m ⁡ \times 4} = \dfrac{9 \times 2}{2 \times 4}$

100697.subject: Physics
100697.text: Two blocks of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ (where $m_1 > m_2$) are connected by a light inextensible string that passes over a frictionless pulley. If the acceleration of the system is $\dfrac{g}{2}$, what is the ratio of their masses ($m_1 : m_2$)?
100697.sol:
For an Atwood machine with masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ ($m_1 > m_2$), the acceleration $a$ is given by:

$a = \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g$

Given that $a = \dfrac{g}{2}$, we can write:

$\dfrac{g}{2} = \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g$

Cancelling $g$ from both sides:

$\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}$

Cross-multiplying yields:

$m_1 + m_2 = 2m_1 - 2m_2$

Rearranging the terms:

$3m_2 = m_1$

$\dfrac{m_1}{m_2} = \dfrac{3}{1}$

Thus, the ratio $m_1 : m_2$ is $3 : 1$.

Answer: $3 : 1$

102064.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): On a $P-V$ diagram, the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve for a given ideal gas.
Reason (R): The magnitude of the slope of the isothermal curve is $\gamma$ (ratio of specific heats) times the magnitude of the slope of the adiabatic curve at any given point.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
102064.sol:
The slope of an isothermal process on a $P-V$ diagram is given by $\dfrac{dP}{dV} = -\dfrac{P}{V}$.

The slope of an adiabatic process is given by $\dfrac{dP}{dV} = -\gamma \dfrac{P}{V}$.

Since $\gamma = \dfrac{C_p}{C_v} > 1$ for all ideal gases, the magnitude of the adiabatic slope is $\gamma$ times the magnitude of the isothermal slope. This makes the adiabatic curve steeper than the isothermal curve.

Therefore, the Assertion is correct, but the Reason is incorrect because it incorrectly states that the isothermal slope is $\gamma$ times the adiabatic slope.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

102248.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The mean free path of gas molecules in a closed rigid container remains unchanged when the temperature of the gas is increased.

Reason (R): The mean free path of gas molecules is inversely proportional to the number density of the gas, which remains constant in a closed rigid container.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
102248.sol:
The mean free path of a gas molecule is given by the formula:
$\lambda = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2 n}$
where $d$ is the diameter of the molecule and $n$ is the number density (number of molecules per unit volume, $n = \dfrac{N}{V}$).

In a closed rigid container, both the total number of gas molecules ($N$) and the volume of the container ($V$) remain constant. Therefore, the number density ($n$) of the gas remains constant regardless of any change in temperature.

Since the number density does not change, the mean free path of the gas molecules also remains unchanged. Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) provides the correct explanation for (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

103681.subject: Physics
103681.text: A long straight solid wire of radius $R$ carries a steady current uniformly distributed across its cross-section. The magnitude of the magnetic field is maximum at the surface of the wire and is equal to $B_0$. At what radial distances from the axis of the wire is the magnitude of the magnetic field equal to $\dfrac{B_0}{4}$?
103681.sol:
Let the current in the wire be $I$. The magnetic field is maximum at the surface ($r = R$):
$B_0 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi R}$

Case 1: Inside the wire ($r < R$)
The magnetic field at a distance $r$ is given by $B_{in} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi R^2} = B_0 \left(\dfrac{r}{R}\right)$.
Given $B_{in} = \dfrac{B_0}{4}$, we have:
$B_0 \left(\dfrac{r}{R}\right) = \dfrac{B_0}{4} \implies r = \dfrac{R}{4}$

Case 2: Outside the wire ($r \ge R$)
The magnetic field at a distance $r$ is given by $B_{out} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} = B_0 \left(\dfrac{R}{r}\right)$.
Given $B_{out} = \dfrac{B_0}{4}$, we have:
$B_0 \left(\dfrac{R}{r}\right) = \dfrac{B_0}{4} \implies r = 4R$

Thus, the magnetic field is $\dfrac{B_0}{4}$ at radial distances $\dfrac{R}{4}$ and $4R$.

Answer: $\dfrac{R}{4}$ and $4R$

104560.text: The focal length of the objective and eye lenses of a microscope are \(1.6 \mathrm{~cm}\) and \(2.5 \mathrm{~cm}\) respectively. The distance between the two lenses is \(21.7 \mathrm{~cm}\). If the final image is formed at infinity. What is the linear magnification?
104560.sol:
Here \(v_O=L-f_e=21.7 \mathrm{ cm}-2.5 \mathrm{ cm}=+19.2 \mathrm{ cm}\) \(+v e\) sign shows that image is real.
For a objective lens \(\frac{1}{u_O}+\frac{1}{v_O}=\frac{1}{f_O}\)
[using real-virtual sign convention]
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad \frac{1}{u_O}=\frac{1}{f_O}-\frac{1}{v_O} \quad \therefore \quad \frac{1}{u_O}=\frac{1}{(+1.6)}-\frac{1}{(+19.2)} \\
& \frac{1}{u_O}=\frac{19.2-1.6}{(1.6)(19.2)} \quad \text{$ or $} \quad u_O=+1.745 \mathrm{ cm}
\end{aligned}\)
+ve sign shows that object is real.
When the image is formed at infinity, the magnification is given by
\(m=\left(\frac{v_O}{u_O}\right)\left(\frac{D}{f_e}\right)\)
where \(D\) is the distance of distinct vision.
\(\therefore \quad m=\left(\frac{19.2 \mathrm{ cm}}{1.745 \mathrm{ cm}}\right)\left(\frac{25 \mathrm{ cm}}{2.5 \mathrm{ cm}}\right)=110 .\)$

107708.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The $\text{O}_2$ molecule is paramagnetic because its highest occupied molecular orbitals are $\pi^{*}_{2p_x}$ and $\pi^{*}_{2p_y}$, each containing one electron.
Reason (R): In the $\text{O}_2$ molecule, the energy of the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ molecular orbital is higher than that of the $\pi_{2p_x}$ and $\pi_{2p_y}$ orbitals.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
107708.sol:
The $\text{O}_2$ molecule has 16 electrons. Its molecular orbital electronic configuration is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \ {\sigma^{*}}_{1s}^2 \ \sigma_{2s}^2 \ {\sigma^{*}}_{2s}^2 \ \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \ \pi_{2p_x}^2 = \pi_{2p_y}^2 \ {\pi^{*}}_{2p_x}^1 = {\pi^{*}}_{2p_y}^1$

The highest occupied molecular orbitals are $\pi^{*}_{2p_x}$ and $\pi^{*}_{2p_y}$, each containing one unpaired electron. The presence of these unpaired electrons makes the $\text{O}_2$ molecule paramagnetic. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.

For molecules with more than 14 electrons (like $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{F}_2$), the $2s$-$2p$ mixing is negligible. As a result, the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ molecular orbital is lower in energy than the $\pi_{2p_x}$ and $\pi_{2p_y}$ orbitals. Thus, Reason (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

113878.subject: Chemistry
113878.text:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Liquid Mixture)List II (Solution Behavior)
A. Ethanol + AcetoneI. Ideal solution
B. Nitric acid + WaterII. Positive deviation from Raoult's law
C. Bromoethane + ChloroethaneIII. Negative deviation from Raoult's law

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
113878.sol:
According to Raoult's law and the properties of liquid mixtures:

A. Ethanol and acetone mixture shows a positive deviation from Raoult's law (A-II). In pure ethanol, molecules are hydrogen bonded. On adding acetone, its molecules get in between the host molecules and break some of these hydrogen bonds, weakening the overall intermolecular interactions.

B. Nitric acid and water mixture shows a negative deviation from Raoult's law (B-III). This is because the new interactions (hydrogen bonding) between nitric acid and water are stronger than the interactions in the pure components.

C. Bromoethane and chloroethane have nearly identical structures and polarities. The intermolecular attractive forces between A-A and B-B are nearly equal to A-B interactions, thus forming an ideal solution (C-I).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-III, C-I.

Answer: A-II, B-III, C-I

119300.subject: Chemistry
119300.text: When 2,6-octanedione is heated with dilute aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, it undergoes intramolecular aldol condensation to form a mixture of products. Which of the following pairs represents the two possible six-membered cyclic $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketones formed in this reaction?
119300.sol:
The reactant is 2,6-octanedione: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$.
It has four enolizable $\alpha$-carbons: C1, C3, C5, and C7. Intramolecular aldol condensation favors the formation of stable five- or six-membered rings.

Case 1: Enolate formation at C1 and attack on C6.
The C1 carbanion attacks the C6 carbonyl carbon, forming a 6-membered ring. After dehydration, a double bond forms between C1 and C6. The original C2 becomes the ring carbonyl (C1'). The C6 carbon (now C3' of the ring) retains the ethyl group ($\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_3$). This yields 3-ethylcyclohex-2-en-1-one.

Case 2: Enolate formation at C7 and attack on C2.
The C7 carbanion attacks the C2 carbonyl carbon, forming another 6-membered ring. Dehydration creates a double bond between C7 and C2. The original C6 becomes the ring carbonyl (C1'). The C7 carbon (now C2' of the ring) has a methyl group (from C8), and the C2 carbon (now C3' of the ring) has a methyl group (from C1). This yields 2,3-dimethylcyclohex-2-en-1-one.

Attacks from C3 or C5 would lead to highly strained four-membered rings, which are not formed. Thus, the two six-membered products are 3-ethylcyclohex-2-en-1-one and 2,3-dimethylcyclohex-2-en-1-one.

Answer: 3-Ethylcyclohex-2-en-1-one and 2,3-dimethylcyclohex-2-en-1-one

121511.subject: Botany
121511.text:
Type of Bacteria/CharacteristicDescription
A. Eubacteria1. Smallest living cells, lack a cell wall
B. Cyanobacteria2. Rigid cell wall, can be motile with a flagellum
C. Mycoplasma3. Photosynthetic autotrophs, can fix atmospheric nitrogen
D. Heterotrophic bacteria4. Decomposers, involved in nitrogen fixation, some are pathogens
121511.sol:
A - 2: Eubacteria are characterized by a rigid cell wall and, if motile, have a flagellum. These are considered the "true bacteria."
B - 3: Cyanobacteria are also known as blue-green algae. They are photosynthetic autotrophs with chlorophyll a and can also fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called heterocysts (e.g., Nostoc and Anabaena).
C - 1: Mycoplasma are unique in that they are the smallest living cells known and lack a cell wall. They can survive without oxygen and many are pathogenic.
D - 4: Heterotrophic bacteria are the most abundant bacteria in nature, primarily functioning as decomposers. They are involved in processes such as nitrogen fixation (in the roots of legumes), and some species are pathogenic, causing diseases like cholera, typhoid, tetanus, and citrus canker.

122180.subject: Botany
122180.text: What is the basis for animal classification?
122180.sol: Inspite of differences in structure and form of different animals, there are fundamental features common to various individuals in relation to the arrangement of cells, body symmetry, nature of coelom, patterns of digestive, circulatory or reproductive systems. These features are used as the basis of animal classification Though all members of Animalia are multicellular, all of them do not exhibit the same pattern of organisation of cells. For example, in sponges, the cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates, i.e., they exhibit cellular level of organisation. Some division of labour (activities) occur among the cells. In coelenterates, the arrangement of cells is more complex. Here the cells performing the same function are arranged into tissues, hence is called tissue level of organisation. A still higher level of organisation, i.e., organ level is exhibited by members of Platyhelminthes and other higher phyla where tissues are grouped together to form organs, each specialised for a particular function.

123030.text: A student is recording the floral characters of two plants, Cassia and cucumber. Which of the following options correctly represents the floral symbol for the symmetry of Cassia flowers and the ovary position of cucumber flowers, respectively?
123030.sol:
Cassia flowers can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane, meaning they exhibit bilateral symmetry (zygomorphic). The symbol for zygomorphic symmetry is $\%$.

Cucumber flowers are epigynous, meaning the margin of the thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it, while other floral parts arise above the ovary. This makes the ovary inferior. The symbol for an inferior ovary is $\overline{G}$.

Therefore, the correct combination is $\%$ and $\overline{G}$.

Answer: $\%$ and $\overline{G}$

123533.subject: Botany
123533.text: How does cell growth occur during the cell cycle?
options: By the formation of new cells
By the division of existing cells
By the synthesis of new cell components
123533.sol: Cell division is a very important process in all living organisms. During the division of a cell, DNA replication and cell growth also take place. All these processes, i.e., cell division, DNA replication, and cell growth, hence, have to take place in a coordinated way to ensure correct division and formation of progeny cells containing intact genomes. The sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises the other constituents of the cell and eventually divides into two daughter cells is termed cell cycle. Although cell growth (in terms of cytoplasmic increase) is a continuous process, DNA synthesis occurs only during one specific stage in the cell cycle.

125947.subject: Botany
125947.text: In which type of plants is endosperm completely consumed before seed maturation?
125947.sol: Endosperm development precedes embryo development. Why? The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly and forms a triploid endosperm tissue. Subsequently cell wall formation occurs and the endosperm becomes cellular. The number of free nuclei formed before cellularisation varies greatly. The coconut water from tender coconut that you are familiar with, is nothing but free-nuclear endosperm (made up of thousands of nuclei) and the surrounding white kernel is the cellular endosperm. Endosperm may either be completely consumed by the developing embryo (e.g., pea, groundnut, beans) before seed maturation or it may persist in the mature seed (e.g. castor and coconut) and be used up during seed germination. Split open some seeds of castor, peas, beans, groundnut, fruit of coconut and look for the endosperm in each case. Find out whether the endosperm is persistent in cereals – wheat, rice and maize.

125990.subject: Botany
125990.text: What is the impact of apomixis on hybrid seed cost?
options: It decreases the cost of hybrid seeds
It increases the cost of hybrid seeds
It has no effect on the cost
It makes hybrid seeds less effective
125990.sol: Hybrid varieties of several of our food and vegetable crops are being extensively cultivated. Cultivation of hybrids has tremendously increased productivity. If the seeds collected from hybrids are sown, the plants in the progeny will segregate and do not maintain hybrid characters. Production of hybrid seeds is costly and hence the cost of hybrid seeds become too expensive for the farmers. If these hybrids are made into apomicts, there is no segregation of characters in the hybrid progeny. Then the farmers can keep on using the hybrid seeds to raise new crop year after year and he does not have to buy hybrid seeds every year. Because of the importance of apomixis in hybrid seed industry, active research is going on in many laboratories around the world to understand the genetics of apomixis and to transfer apomictic genes into hybrid varieties.

128092.sol:
The inner lining of the stomach and intestine is composed of simple columnar epithelium, which helps in secretion and absorption.

According to NCERT, simple columnar epithelium is composed of a single layer of tall and slender cells, and their nuclei are characteristically located at the base, making the first option correct.

The second option is incorrect because the nuclei in columnar cells are basal, not central. The third option is incorrect as simple cuboidal epithelium is typically found in ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons, not the stomach lining. The fourth option is incorrect because compound epithelium is multi-layered and covers surfaces subjected to mechanical or chemical stress (like the buccal cavity or pharynx), whereas the stomach and intestine require a single-layered epithelium for efficient secretion and absorption.

Answer: Simple columnar epithelium; composed of a single layer of tall and slender cells with their nuclei located at the base

131317.sol:
The process of delivery of the foetus (childbirth) is called parturition. Parturition is induced by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism. The signals for parturition originate from the fully developed foetus and the placenta which induce mild uterine contractions called foetal ejection reflex.

132510.subject: Zoology
132510.text: The diploid somatic chromosome number in a female bird of a particular species is $78$. What will be the exact chromosome composition of the ova produced by this bird?
132510.sol:
Birds exhibit the ZZ-ZW type of sex determination, where females are heterogametic (possessing one Z and one W chromosome) and males are homogametic (ZZ).

The given diploid chromosome number ($2n$) of the female bird is $78$. This total includes both autosomes and sex chromosomes.

Number of autosomes = Total chromosomes - Sex chromosomes = $78 - 2 = 76$ autosomes ($76\text{A}$).

During meiosis, the chromosome number is halved to form haploid gametes (ova). The $76$ autosomes segregate equally, resulting in $38$ autosomes ($38\text{A}$) per ovum.

Since the female is heterogametic (ZW), she will produce two types of ova in equal proportion: one carrying the Z chromosome and the other carrying the W chromosome.

Therefore, the exact chromosome composition of the two types of ova will be $38\text{A} + \text{Z}$ and $38\text{A} + \text{W}$.

Answer: $38\text{A} + \text{Z}$ and $38\text{A} + \text{W}$
